recommendations.regimenLabel: Rate control (IV beta-blocker) then BP control + analgesia
steps: EMERGENCY — CT angiogram of the aorta; involve cardiothoracic surgery.
Control HR then BP: IV beta-blocker (labetalol/esmolol) to HR <60 and SBP ~100–120, add vasodilator.
Type A (ascending): emergency surgery. Type B: usually medical ± endovascular for complications.

drugRefs.dose: 20 mg IV bolus, repeat/double every 10 min (max ~300 mg) or infusion 1–2 mg/min
drugRefs.freq: titrated to HR <60 and SBP ~100–120 mmHg
drugRefs.why: Reduces aortic wall shear stress (dP/dt); rate control must precede vasodilatation to avoid reflex tachycardia and propagation.

drugRefs.dose: 500 mcg/kg IV over 1 min, then infusion 50–200 mcg/kg/min
drugRefs.why: Ultra-short-acting; easily titratable rate control, useful if haemodynamic instability or need for rapid on/off control.
Further lowers BP once heart rate is controlled; must never be given before beta-blockade (reflex tachycardia increases dP/dt).
Controls pain and the associated sympathetic surge, helping HR/BP control.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection
2014 ESC Guidelines on the Diagnosis and Treatment of Aortic Diseases
2022 ACC/AHA Guideline for the Diagnosis and Management of Aortic Disease

decision.label: Emergency — HR then BP control + surgery for Type A

confirm: Sudden tearing chest/back pain ± pulse/BP differential, new aortic regurgitation, widened mediastinum. CT angiography aorta.
